SMTO-HTTP-0072 — The data SMTO tried to send is too large

GUID: bb92dbd2-58e1-4abc-9573-f991a27da888
Slug: http-request-body-limit
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO tried to send more than about 1 MB of data in a single request to a web service. It stopped before sending anything and did not cut the data short.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to send the data in smaller parts, for example a few records per request. Each single request is limited to about 1 MB, so smaller parts fit under the limit.
  2. If the data is a document or other file and the service accepts uploads, ask SMTO to send it as a file upload instead. File uploads use a separate path that is not held to the 1 MB limit for ordinary requests.
  3. If you split the work, ask SMTO to check which parts the service already has before sending the rest. This avoids sending the same records twice if some parts succeed and others don't.

What success looks like

  • Each smaller request or the upload finishes and the step shows the service's reply.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete earlier results or your input to make the request smaller.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • prepare_request rejected the request because the encoded non-upload body exceeds the 1 MiB native HTTP body limit.

What this means

  • The encoded non-upload request body exceeds the one MiB native HTTP body limit. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The encoded non-upload request body exceeds the one MiB native HTTP body limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Measure encoded body bytes and distinguish the separate authorized file-upload path.

How to fix it

  • Keep json_body, form_body and text bodies under 1 MiB (MAX_BODY_BYTES in gateway_core/http_contract.py). Split the work into smaller requests the endpoint supports, or send large content through the upload modes (multipart_body or body_reference); never truncate the body silently.
  • Reduce or batch the operation using the endpoint-supported format, or use the supported upload/reference path. Do not silently truncate the body.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A provider-supported smaller body or approved upload form fits its own bound.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
